texts.preamble: Ramesh vs Brij Nandan Yadav And Ors on 21 December, 2024 In The Court Of Shri Sudeep Raj Saini Presiding Officer, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal02 Southwest District, Dwarka Courts, New Delhi In the matter of: Ramesh vs. Brij Nandan Yadav & Ors. Mact No. 2292/2016 Ramesh S/o Late Sh. Naresh Mahto H. No. T49, Gali No. 1, Tukhmir Pur North East, Delhi110094 ....Petitioner Versus 1. Brij Nandan Yadav (Driver) S/o Sh. Sagar Yadav R/o Village Garhi Bishanpur Post Office Kiul P.S. & District Lakhisarai Bihar 2. D.A.V. College Managing Committee (Owner) Through the Principal, D.A.V. Public School P.S. & District Lakhisarai Bihar 3. The Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. (Insurer) Having its office at: Pankaj Plaza, Plot No. 4 Second Floor, Sector4 Dwarka, New Delhi.
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed the present claim petition under sections 166 & 140 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereafter 'M V Act') to seek compensation for the injuries suffered by him in a road accident. The respondent no. 1 Sh. Brij Nandan Yadav is the driver and the respondent no. 2 D.A.V. College Managing Committee through the Principal, D.A.V. Public School, Lakhisarai is the owner of the alleged offending vehicle/bus bearing registration no. BR53 2429. The respondent no. 3, The Oriental Insurance Company Limited, is the insurer of the said offending bus. Claim Petition 2. It is claimed by the petitioner that on 08.07.2016 at about 07.00 am, the petitioner along with his father Sh. Naresh Mahto and his uncle (fufa) Sh. Ramprasad Mahto was going for Ganga Snan from his native village Kiul Basti, Pachna Road, PS Kawaiya OP, District Lakhisarai on motorcycle bearing registration no. BR 2A 3907. The motorcycle was being driven by the petitioner while Sh. Naresh Mahto and Sh. Ramprasad Mahto were riding pillion . When they reached near village Balgodar, NH80, Pitch Road, Post & District Lakhisarari, the offending bus bearing registration no. BR532429, being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and at high speed, hit the motorcycle. Due to the impact, the motorcycle fell down and all three of them suffered injuries. They were removed to Sadar Hospital, Lakhisarai, Bihar. Sh. Ramprasad Mahto succumbed to the injuries suffered in the accident on the same day. Sh. Naresh Mahto was admitted to Perfect Life Care Hospital & Research Centre, Patna from 09.07.2016 to 22.07.2016 and thereafter at Lok Nayak Hospital, Delhi where he expired on 16.08.2016. The petitioner remained admitted at Perfect Life Care Hospital & Research Centre, Patna from 08.07.2016 and was discharged on 22.07.2016 after receiving treatment for grievous injuries. The petitioner has claimed a sum of Rs. 25,00,000/ (Rupees Twenty Five Lacs) from respondents as compensation along with interest from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization. Defence of the Respondents 3. Notice of the petition was served on the respondents. The respondents no. 1 & 2 have filed their respective written statements, which are on similar lines. Respondents no. 1 & 2 have objected to the petition on the ground of territorial jurisdiction. Respondents no.1& 2 have claimed that the respondent no. 1 was having valid and effective driving license on the day of the accident. Respondents no. 1 & 2 have further claimed that the accident was caused as the driver of the motorcycle lost his balance, as three persons were riding a motorcycle which has seating capacity of two, and came before the bus. The respondents no. 1 & 2 have claimed that the offending bus was insured with respondent no. 3/ Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. The respondent no. 3 admitted that the alleged offending bus was insured with it on the day of accident. The respondent no. 3 has claimed that it is a case of triple riding on the motorcycle and the injured, being the driver of motorcycle, is also guilty of negligence as the motorcycle is a twoseater vehicle. The respondent no. 3 has also claimed statutory defences under sections 149(2) and 170 of Ramesh vs Brij Nandan Yadav And Ors on 21 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24482883/ 2 MV Act. Inquiry 4. The present claim petition, claim petition bearing MACT no. 2290/2016 titled Vimla Devi & Ors. vs. Brij Nandan Yadav & Ors. and claim petition bearing MACT no. 2291/2016 titled Rina Devi vs. Brij Nandan Yadav & Ors. arise from the same accident. As common questions of law and facts were involved, so these petitions were consolidated for the purpose of recording of evidence with the claim petition bearing MACT no. 2290/2016 as the leading petition vide order dated 08.08.2018 of my ld. predecessor. OPP. (3) Relief. Thereafter, the claim petition was fixed for petitioner's evidence. 5. In order to prove his claim, the petitioner has examined three witnesses. 6. Smt. Vimla Devi (the petitioner no.1 in aforesaid MACT no. 2290/2016) appeared as PW1 and filed her evidence by way of affidavit and the same is Ex. PW1/A. She deposed regarding the income and employment of Sh. Naresh Mahto. The PW1 has relied upon following documents in support of her testimony: Ex. PW1/1 (colly) is the certified copy of chargesheet. Ex. PW1/2 is the Death Report dated 18.08.2016 of death of Sh. Naresh Mahto. Ex. PW1/3 is the copy of the entry regarding Sh. Naresh Mahto in Medico Legal Injury Register of Medical Record Department, Lok Nayak Hospital. The petitioner has also examined Smt. Reena Devi (the petitioner no.1 in aforesaid MACT No. 2291/2016) as PW2 who filed her evidence by way of affidavit and the same is Ex. PW2/A. She deposed regarding the income and employment of Sh. Ramprasad Mahto. PW2 has relied upon following documents in support of her testimony: Ex. PW2/1 is copy of death certificate of deceased Sh. Ramprasad Mahto. Mental & Physical Shock Rs. 25,000/ Total Rs. 2,97,408/ Deduction on Account of Contributory Negligence 33. The respondents no. 1 & 2, being the principal tortfeasors, are primarily liable to make payment of compensation awarded to the petitioner.
texts.arguments: 14. The respondents no. 1 & 2 have opposed the claim by contending that this Tribunal lacks the territorial jurisdiction to adjudicate the present claim petition as the accident took place in Bihar. 15. The respondents have also opposed the claim on the ground that the accident was caused as the driver of the motorcycle lost his balance as three persons were riding the motorcycle which has seating capacity of two. 16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Bimla Devi and Others vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and Others (2009) 13 SCC 530 has held: "15.In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter. It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the Ramesh vs Brij Nandan Yadav And Ors on 21 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24482883/ 5 claimants. 17. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mangla Ram vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited and Others(2018) 5 Supreme Court Cases 656 has laid down in paragraphs 27 & 28: "27. ...This Court in a recent decision in Dulcina Fernandes, noted that the key of negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle as set up by the claimants was required to be decided by the Tribunal on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and certainly not by standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt. 18. The Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in National Insurance Company Ltd. Versus Smt. Pushpa Rana & Ors.2008 (101) DRJ 645 has held: "12. The last contention of the appellant insurance company is that the respondents claimants should have proved negligence on the part of the driver and in this regard the counsel has placed reliance on the judgement of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Meena Variyal; 2007 (5) SCALE 269. These documents Ramesh vs Brij Nandan Yadav And Ors on 21 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24482883/ 6 are sufficient proofs to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent. 20. As far as the contention of the respondents no. 1 & 2 regarding territorial jurisdiction is concerned, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Malati Sardar Versus National Insurance Company Limited And Others (2016) 3 SCC 43 has held: "16. The provision in question, in the present case, is a benevolent provision for the victims of accidents of negligent driving. The High Court failed to notice the provision of Section 21 CPC." 21. As far as the contention of the respondents regarding triple riding is concerned, a similar question arose for the consideration of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mohammed Siddique & Anr. vs. National Insurance Company Ltd. & Ors. [2020] 1 S.C.R. 931 wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court held: "13. But the above reason, in our view, is flawed. The fact that the deceased was riding on a motor cycle along with the driver and another, may not, by itself, without anything more, make him guilty of contributory negligence. At the most it would make him guilty of being a party to the violation of the law. Section 128 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, imposes a restriction on the driver of a twowheeled motor cycle, Ramesh vs Brij Nandan Yadav And Ors on 21 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24482883/ 7 not to carry more than one person on the motor cycle. Section 194C inserted by the Amendment Act 32 of 2019, prescribes a penalty for violation of safety measures for motor cycle drivers and pillion riders. Therefore, the fact that a person was a pillion rider on a motor cycle along with the driver and one more person on the pillion, may be a violation of the law. There must either be a causal connection between the violation and the accident or a causal connection between the violation and the impact of the accident upon the victim. 26. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 343 has laid down the general principles relating to compensation in injury cases and held: "6. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) Ramesh vs Brij Nandan Yadav And Ors on 21 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24482883/ 9 (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. Nonpecuniary damages (General damages) (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). The Hon'ble Supreme Court vide its order dated 16.07.2024 in Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Private Ltd. vs. Union Of India & Ors. 41. The said Manager is further directed that: (a) The Bank shall not permit any joint name(s) to be added in the aforesaid MACT account or fixed deposit account(s) of the petitioner no.1.
